content:
maya: Quick runbook for a focused experiment on max-tokens-per-batch / max-batch tuning across A10, T4, L4, A100, H100. Goal: find stable token-budget targets that hit p50 latency SLOs while maximizing throughput and avoiding KV-cache thrash.

maya: Plan summary: 1) Run isolated loadtests per GPU type with a realistic request length distribution (p25=32, p50=128, p75=512, p95=2048). 2) Sweep max_tokens_per_batch and max_batch_size. 3) Capture kernel selection traces, KV cache hit/evict events, per-request latency (p50/p95/p99), and best-effort throughput (requests/sec & tokens/sec). 4) Compare with current baseline and flag any regressions in kernel switching or latency tail.

sam: SGTM. What's our baseline configs and the sweep range?

maya: Baseline (current prod-ish):
```
# runtime.cfg snippet
max_tokens_per_batch: 8192
max_batch_size: 64
token_budget_policy: dynamic_margin
kv_cache_policy: prefix_cache_enabled
queue_policy: fifo_with_priority
```
Sweep ranges (per GPU type):
- max_tokens_per_batch: [1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384]
- max_batch_size: [8, 16, 32, 64, 128]
We won't run all combinations for every GPU — pick a focused subset: low/medium/high token budget × small/medium/large batch sizes (9 runs per GPU).

rachel: Add KV cache toggles to the matrix. For A100/H100, KV fragmentation shows in tail latencies when token budgets are large. Include runs with kv_cache_policy: [prefix_cache_enabled, prefix_cache_disabled] for the high-budget configs.

eli: Suggest adding a single enforced kernel pin test: force the kernel selector to pick the faster int8 path (when available) to see how latency vs. token packing trades off. Example command:
```
./test-driver --gpu=A100 --force-kernel=int8_path --max-tokens=8192 --clients=32
```
This will help isolate whether kernel switching is the main culprit.

maya: Good call. Also add a test that mimics KV hotshot scenario: repeated short prefixes that cause heavy KV reuse to ensure caching helps.

perf-bot: Reminder: upload profiling artifacts to s3://redwood-perf/experiments/1728456123/ and attach flamegraphs.

ops-jen: For loadgen, use the staging GPU pools (stg-a10, stg-t4, stg-l4, stg-a100, stg-h100). I’ll reserve time windows 03:00–06:00 UTC tomorrow to avoid interference. Tag me when ready.

sam: Quick question on metrics collection — which traces are mandatory?

maya: Mandatory: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, requests/sec, kernel-selection log, KV cache hits/evicts per minute, GC pauses (if any), GPU util (SM%/mem%), and per-request queuing time. Optional: perf counters (L2 hit/miss) if available.

eli: Proposed abort criteria:
- p95 latency increases >20% vs baseline for the same throughput
- any p99 spikes >2x baseline
- kernel-selection flip that increases p50 by >10% and persists >5 minutes
If any triggered, we stop the sweep and investigate.

rachel: Also watch for increased memory fragmentation on L4/A10 under large batch sizes — we saw OOM-ish allocation failures with 128 batch on L4 last month. Add an OOM / allocation-failure flag.

maya: Experiment run steps (short):
1) Push test config to test repo: experiments/1728456123/run.yml
2) Kick off run via loadgen orchestrator (example):
```
curl -X POST https://stg-loadgen.internal/trigger \
  -d '{"gpu":"A100","config":"s3://.../run.yml","label":"1728456123-a100-high"}'
```
3) Perf-bot will annotate and upload artifacts.
4) Collect metrics + kernel logs + KV traces, then run our analysis notebook to compute cost/latency frontier.

sam: Can you paste the minimal run.yml we should start with?

maya: Minimal: (shortened)
```
name: batchsize-token-sweep
gpu: ${GPU}
clients: 32
duration: 1800  # seconds
request_distribution:
  p25: 32
  p50: 128
  p75: 512
  p95: 2048
sweep:
  max_tokens_per_batch: [2048, 8192, 16384]
  max_batch_size: [16, 64]
policies:
  token_budget_policy: dynamic_margin
  kv_cache_policy: prefix_cache_enabled
```

eli: Note: for T4 we may need to reduce clients to 16 to avoid saturating SMs artificially.

rachel: I'll add a small helper to parse kernel logs for frequency of kernel flips. If flips > threshold (say >5 flips/minute) we mark run noisy.

perf-bot: Upload status: queued -> will autotag artifacts with labels: gpu, max_tokens, batch_size, kv_policy.

maya: Expected deliverables after the run:
- CSV of all runs with metrics (tokens/sec, req/sec, p50/p95/p99, KV hit%, kernel_flip_rate)
- Short writeup with recommended default token_budget and max_batch_size per GPU with rationale (e.g., "A100: prefer max_tokens=16384 + batch=64 for long-token workloads; L4: cap tokens to 4096 and batch=32 to avoid mem fragmentation")
- Flagged any kernel regression tickets (link to Jira) and follow-ups.

sam: Would be useful to include cost-per-token estimate for each config (approx GPU-hours * token/sec) so product can make informed defaults.

maya: Agreed. We'll add a cost_column in the CSV using internal pricing model.

ops-jen: I'm reserving stg-A100 03:00–04:00 UTC and stg-H100 04:00–05:00 UTC. Send me final run labels and I'll approve.

rachel: One more: instrument KV cache to emit per-prefix hit latency histograms — sometimes hits are expensive on large caches and hurt tail.

maya: Noted. I'll push the updated run.yml including that.

perf-bot: Run started: 1728456301-A100-high (ETA 30m). Artifacts will appear in s3 when complete. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sam: Thanks — will watch the dashboard.

perf-bot: Run finished: 1728456789-A100-high. p50=48ms, p95=210ms, p99=640ms, tokens/sec=2.1M, kernel_flip_rate=0.2/min, kv_hit% = 86%. Artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/experiments/1728456123/a100-high/*.

maya: Initial read: p95 looks acceptable, but p99 still high for some long-token tails. Eli, can you inspect kernel logs where kernel_flip_rate spikes correlate with p99?

eli: Looking now. Quick grep shows a ~3 minute window where kernel selector fell back from int8_path to fallback_fp16 for sequences >12k tokens — likely due to memory fragmentation. Patching a smaller allocator slab for the test reduced flips in a follow-up short run.

rachel: That's telling — memory allocator behavior interacts with kernel selection. We should add allocator slab target as a tunable for L4/A10.

maya: Good. Next steps: 1) run T4/L4 sweeps with allocator slab tuning, 2) collect KV-on/off comparisons for heavy prefix reuse, 3) produce recommendation doc. I’ll create the follow-up thread with results table.

ops-jen: Approved windows: I'm green for the next runs. Ping me when scheduling.

sam: Thanks everyone. I’ll help assemble the CSV and cost calc once artifacts are uploaded.

maya: Thanks — closing this thread for runbook. Will post results + recommended defaults in follow-up. :white_check_mark:
